title: Initiative Queue — Cost‑Weighted Latency Sensitivity and RICE Calibration
creator: Asha Patel
description: Introduce an initiative-queue scoring playbook that augments standard RICE with a cost-weighted latency sensitivity dimension. The goal is to give PMs and Eng leads a repeatable calibration for prioritizing features where token cost and tail latency have outsized product impact. This ticket scopes the scoring rubric, calibration experiments against historical roadmap decisions, a lightweight spreadsheet prototype, and integration guidance for cycle planning. It also captures trade-offs for different weighting strategies (strict cost vs user-facing latency vs reliability).
motivation: Existing RICE variants at Redwood surface impact and reach but underweight per-token economics and latency SLO violations. As Dedicated and Private customers scale, we need a prioritization signal that reflects unit economics and operational risk without penalizing high-impact UX work unduly.
proposal_summary: Create a calibrated score = RICE_base * LatencySensitivityFactor * CostAdjustment, where LatencySensitivityFactor is derived from SLO breach probability and customer exposure, and CostAdjustment converts per-feature incremental token spend into a multiplicative penalty. Provide example buckets and calibration guidance (low/medium/high sensitivity) and backtest over Q4 2024 feature set.
acceptance_criteria: Rubric doc published in Confluence with sample calculations and bucket definitions
Spreadsheet prototype populated with 15 historical roadmap items and backtest results included
Calibration recommendations (low/medium/high) agreed by PM, Eng infra lead, and GTO owner
Integration notes for Linear/roadmap import (CSV template) submitted
One stakeholder review session completed with recorded decisions and next steps

comments: 2025-02-12: Asha created initial draft; included rationale and initial checklist. Assigned to Maya for scoping and calibration.

2025-02-14: Maya: Met with Runtime infra (Derek) to align on SLO signals we can use programmatically (p50/p95/p99 latency, error-rate, SLO-breach count). Derek suggested using a 30-day breach probability metric rather than raw p99 to reduce noise.

2025-02-16: PM review: Suggested reducing the cost penalty scaling for experiments and UX flows — otherwise UX initiatives were being deprioritized in the backtest. Added a proposed floor to CostAdjustment to preserve breakthrough UX work.

2025-02-17: Eng feedback: PR created to add sensitivity and token_cost_delta columns to roadmap importer; noted that some historical items lack token estimates and we will add a 'proxy token bucket' methodology.

2025-02-18: Calibration session with Design, Eng, and Legal. Decision: three sensitivity tiers (Low/Med/High) with explicit examples. Follow-ups: Product to produce mapping examples; Eng to provide automated SLO telemetry export by 2025-03-05.

2025-02-19: Added backtest summary to sheet (15 items). Early finding: when CostAdjustment weight > 1.2, infra-heavy items shift earlier; recommended default weight = 0.9 for 2025-Q2 planning to avoid overcorrection. Ready for stakeholder sign-off.
risks_and_tradeoffs: Overweighting token cost can bias roadmap towards low-immediacy infra projects and away from high-UX wins
Latency sensitivity signals are noisy; using a breach-probability aggregation reduces flips but may mask sudden regressions
Requires consistent token-estimate discipline on features; otherwise the score will be inaccurate
implementation_notes: Spreadsheet formula examples included: Score = (Reach * Impact * Confidence) / Effort * LatencyFactor * CostFactor
LatencyFactor mapping: Low=1.0, Medium=0.92, High=0.78 by default (tunable)
CostFactor mapping: delta_token_monthly -> multiplier via piecewise function with floor 0.6 and cap 1.25
Backtest instructions: run on previous cycle items with token_estimates filled; record movement in ranking and compute correlation with actual decision order
